items.title: Inventory every count-claim guard that actually binds at HEAD, as a rerunnable tool
items.acceptance: An executable at tools/guard-inventory.mjs re-derives, from the repo at run time (never from hardcoded literals), a table of every guard in test/ whose subject is a numeric or structural COUNT claim about a document: for each one it names the file, the test title, the document claim it reads, where the expected value comes from (derived from src/corpus.js at test time vs. a literal written into the test file), and whether any guard asserts a floor on the SIZE of the suite itself. It also emits the current test-file line count per file and the total. The output must explicitly record the verdict on the inherited '>= 121 tests' floor premise: present or absent, with the evidence that settles it.
items.notes: PLAN confirmed by reading that NO literal suite-size floor exists in test/ — '121' occurs only in two prose comments in readme-matrix-consistency.test.js, and .github/workflows/test.yml carries an explicit written refusal to add a count assertion. So S-1's 'retire the COUNT floor' half likely has nothing to retire and W-2 is net-NEW tooling, not a replacement. The tool must SAY that rather than manufacture a floor to retire. Measured start: 129 tests across 7 files (readme-tags 31, args 28, cli 29, select 18, pipe 16, readme-matrix-consistency 5, node-support-citation 2); test/ 4,587 lines; src+bin 594. tools/ is outside the cited pathspec so creating it cannot falsify the README citation.

items.title: Build the detection floor: bounded, rule-generated mutation matrix with an identity control, baselined at 20b7ede
items.acceptance: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs exists, is zero-dependency, is NOT collected by the suite's own file glob, and adds zero tests. It states its generation rule in the file itself and enumerates at most 30 mutations produced by that rule — exactly one falsifying mutation per machine-checked document claim the W-1 inventory found — plus exactly ONE identity (no-op) mutation as converse control. For each mutation it applies the edit to a scratch copy, runs the suite there, records which NAMED guards fired, and leaves the working tree byte-identical. The identity control must leave the suite green; a mutation no guard catches is reported as SILENT, never omitted. Any claim the generation rule produces but the harness skips is listed with its reason. The baseline result against 20b7ede is recorded in tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json in a machine-comparable shape.
items.notes: Risk: ~30 suite runs. The suite spawns the real binary (cli/pipe tests) and shells out to git (node-support-citation), so the scratch copy must be a real git work tree or those two guards skip/fail for ENVIRONMENTAL reasons rather than because of the mutation — which would corrupt the matrix. Decide and STATE how the scratch copy handles git (clone vs worktree vs accept skips and mark N/A). Baseline at 20b7ede per S-1; HEAD 912a2a4 changed only .swarm/, so src/bin/test should be identical — confirm, do not assume.

items.title: Quote README's citation-selection rule verbatim in the history doc; check it from tools/, not a new test
items.acceptance: docs/node-support-citation-history.md contains README.md's citation-selection-rule sentence as an EXACT substring, attributed to README's '### Node support' section, in place of the current restatement; any surviving description of a superseded rule is clearly marked as history. The doc shows the derivation of applying the QUOTED rule to this tree and lands on the citation the README actually carries. A machine check of at most 30 added lines lives at tools/citation-rule-check.mjs (NOT a new test file), asserts file-to-file substring equality, is demonstrated failable (red when the quote is perturbed) and attributable (its failure names which document diverged), and is paired with a converse control showing it passes on the honest text.
items.notes: Divergence verified in SHAPE: README says the reference matrix is 'the matrix run for the push that carried the last change to src/, bin/, test/, or the workflow itself'; the history file's Q-8 entry states it as 'the most recent run whose cited commit's ... content is byte-identical to this tree's, without requiring that the cited commit be the one that produced the change.' Those select differently once later pushes exist that did not touch the pathspec. NOT executed against the Actions API — re-derive before acting. CONVENTION CONSTRAINT: the file's header promises the five blockquoted cycle entries are byte-identical to text removed from the README and must NOT be edited; the Q-7 and Q-8 entries are not blockquotes and ARE the editable surface. Putting the check in tools/ rather than test/ is deliberate: a sixth README guard test file is the run's explicit anti-goal, and docs/ + tools/ are outside the cited pathspec so this cannot open a citation window.

items.title: Count the citation two-commit tax over repo history, as a rerunnable tool that changes nothing
items.acceptance: tools/citation-tax.mjs walks committed history and derives, without hardcoding the answer: (a) how many commits touched the cited pathspec src/ bin/ test/ .github; (b) of those, how many landed while the citation guard existed and therefore made the README's cited diff non-empty at that commit — knowingly committed RED; (c) how many separate follow-up commits were spent re-citing; (d) the commit gap between each breakage and its repair, so same-commit and later-cycle repairs are distinguishable. It prints the exact derivation per event (breaking SHA, repairing SHA, gap) and ends with a plain recommendation on whether the ritual is intrinsic to a self-falsifying claim or an artifact of an over-claiming pathspec. It changes no pathspec, no assertion, no citation.
items.notes: PLAN's starting measurements, to be RE-DERIVED not trusted: 48 of 255 commits touch the pathspec across all history, but the guard only came into existence at 5f833ab, so 'every commit in history' is the wrong denominator and would inflate the tax. Honest denominator looks like the 6 pathspec-touching commits from 5f833ab forward (5f833ab, c08562b, c9dd7ff, 2b003ea, 4b63e91, 22fdeac→a302f71→7e50d6f), each of which appears to have cost a re-citation commit — i.e. ~100%. The guard also CHANGED SHAPE mid-history (c08562b made it fail loud on ambiguity; 2b003ea added the working-tree comparison), so 'would have turned red' is only well-defined against the guard version live at that commit — decide and state the convention.

items.title: Adjudicate the README Node-support matrix's 127-vs-129 numbers by measurement, as a rerunnable tool
items.acceptance: tools/matrix-adjudication.mjs re-derives, offline and from this checkout: (a) the four matrix rows as README states them; (b) how many tests the suite actually contains at HEAD and how many are the citation guard's two environment-conditional cases; (c) whether the cited base commit's src/bin/test/.github content is identical to this tree's, i.e. whether the citation rule still selects the cited run; (d) an explicit verdict — CORRECT-AS-CITED / STALE / UNDECIDABLE-OFFLINE — with the arithmetic that separates a stale current-state claim from a correctly-cited past-CI claim. If and ONLY IF the verdict is STALE is anything in README.md repaired.
items.notes: PREMISE CHECK from PLAN, recorded rather than planned around: S-5's framing is probably WRONG. The README rows report a REMOTE CI run, and CI checks out at depth 1, so the two node-support-citation tests SKIP there: 129/127/0/2. A local full clone runs those same two and they pass: 129/129/0/0. Both numbers are true of different environments; README's own standing limit 1 says exactly this, and readme-matrix-consistency.test.js's header already spells out why a local run cannot honestly be compared to the table. Most likely honest outcome is CORRECT-AS-CITED with a published explanation and ZERO README edits — which S-5 explicitly calls a PASS. The tool must be ABLE to reach STALE, but must not go looking for a repair. Offline anchor: archived CI evidence under .swarm/runs/ (cycle-005-verify-Q-8.txt names run 32405521233). Network/gh availability unverified — the tool must work without them.

items.title: Close KI-R6-3: consolidate the two guards reading the same 'Tags on exactly one entry' row, or publish the mutation that separates them
items.acceptance: The mutation falsifying README's 'Tags on exactly one entry' counts-table row is run through the detection floor and the set of NAMED guards it fires is recorded. If the two guards' firing sets are identical, exactly ONE is removed, and re-running the matrix shows every mutation detected at the 20b7ede baseline is still detected and the identity control still green. If the firing sets DIFFER, both are kept and the distinguishing mutation — the specific edit one catches and the other does not — is recorded in the test file naming what each guard uniquely catches. Either outcome closes it; 'keep both because removing one feels risky' does not. A drop in test count is a PASS.
items.notes: The two guards are in test/readme-tags.test.js: the test at ~line 434 (Q-4's structural replacement) and the second assertion inside the test at ~line 1598. The file's own comment block at lines 150-162 already concedes they are redundant in the strict sense — 'a wrong value in that row fails both and no mutation fails only one of them' — so consolidation is the likely branch. NOTE removing the ~1598 assertion would also drop the 'Tags on 2 or more entries' check, so target ~434 or be surgical. BIGGEST RISK IN THE PLAN: this is the ONLY item touching test/, inside the cited pathspec, so the commit that lands it makes the README's cited diff non-empty and turns both citation guards RED on a full clone. Closing the window needs a NEW Actions run id, which needs a successful push AND Actions API access — unverified from this environment (origin is https and master is level with origin/master, encouraging but not proof). Sequence LAST among code-touching items, GATE on a confirmed ability to obtain a run id, and predict the window in the commit message per S-8. There is no test/-free path to the removal branch.

items.title: Re-run the detection floor at final HEAD and prove no baseline detection was lost
items.acceptance: The mutation matrix is re-run against final HEAD and recorded in tools/mutation-matrix-final.json in the same machine-comparable shape as the baseline. Any mutation whose FIRING GUARD changed (still detected, by a different named guard) is listed explicitly rather than folded into the pass. items.title: One entry point that re-runs every published finding, so S-6 is checkable rather than asserted
items.acceptance: tools/run-all.mjs invokes every measurement executable this run shipped, in a stated order, prints each one's re-derived output under a labelled heading, and ends with a one-line roll-up of which ran clean and which reported a problem. Zero-dependency, imports nothing outside node: builtins, not collected by the suite, leaves the tree byte-identical. Running it must be sufficient for a skeptical reader to re-derive every number this run publishes WITHOUT reading REPORT.md.

If the mutation matrix is slow (~30 suite runs), give it an opt-out flag and state in the file what the default excludes. This item is the concrete answer to the taste gate's catch that S-1/S-4/S-5 could all be discharged as prose.

items.title: Seven CLI behaviours are unspecified and a human should rule on them (from J-6 + N-4 + D-44 + Q-7 + TS-5)
items.acceptance: A human rules on SEVEN behaviours the Domain rules do not currently decide (two enumerated inline below; five more — D-42, D-43, D-44, D-45, D-46 — enumerated in the notes and written up in SPEC.md § Undecided behaviours), and the ruling is written into SPEC.md as an explicit clause either way. (1) --help vs usage-error precedence when both appear in argv: the shipped behaviour is that the usage error WINS in both argv orders (measured: `--help --seed abc` and `--seed abc --help` both exit 2 with "aphorism: flag --seed requires a numeric value" on stderr). (2) Whether `--seed -0` and `--seed 0` are THE SAME SEED: they are `===` in JavaScript, but toUint32Seed folds the IEEE-754 bit pattern including the sign bit, so they select DIFFERENT aphorisms (measured: seed 0 -> Kernighan "most effective debugging tool"; seed -0 -> Saint-Exupery "Perfection is achieved"). Either behaviour is defensible; the SPEC decides neither.
items.notes:
FILED AT CYCLE 4 from J-6, which measured both and correctly declined to pin either with a test. This is a SPEC decision, not a swarm task, and it is filed the way T-040 is: a human ratifies or reverses, and the item is not dispatchable until they do.

WHY NO TEST WAS ADDED, and why that was right: the Domain rules resolve exactly ONE flag-vs-error precedence question explicitly — for --list ("A seed that fails to parse is still a usage error under --list"). The existence of that carve-out is evidence the author does not treat "usage-error trumps other flags" as self-evidently general; where they meant it to generalise, they said so. They never said it for --help. An assertion pinning today s behaviour would therefore be a future false rejection rather than coverage — which is the failure mode J-6 exists to avoid. Same logic for -0/0: the rule guarantees determinism PER SEED VALUE and says nothing about whether -0 and 0 are one value or two.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RULES ON (2): if the answer is "they are the same seed", that is a PRODUCT bug in toUint32Seed and closing it is a src/ change, which this run s non-goals fence off. If the answer is "they are distinguishable bit patterns, by design", the fix is one SPEC sentence and nothing else. The cheap ruling and the expensive one are not symmetric, so rule before anyone writes code.

HONEST NOTE ON (1) FROM THE BUILDER, disclosed before any gate looked: its "does not map" call on case 1 rests on an INFERENCE from the --list carve-out (silence implies deliberate scoping) rather than on direct textual statement. A reasonable reviewer could read the Exit-codes clause as unconditional and call the current behaviour a hole rather than an unspecified choice. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. | CYCLE 4: N-4 added TWO more rulings to this item, both measured. (3) REPEATED --tag/--author (D-42): shipped behaviour is last-occurrence-wins and it is UNPROTECTED - conductor reproduced it independently (--tag humor --tag design --list prints the 14-entry design list; a first-wins mutant prints the 9-entry humor list; the suite stays 102p/0f on both). SPEC spells every filter flag in the singular and never mentions repetition, so last-wins is an artifact of assignment order in parseArgs, not a contract. (4) EMPTY/WHITESPACE --seed (D-43): SPEC Selection says --seed accepts any value that Number() parses to a non-NaN number, and Number("")===0 is non-NaN, so the literal reading says ACCEPT; the implementation rejects with exit 2 and SPEC Exit-codes calls a missing flag argument bad usage. The two clauses point opposite ways, so there is no decided behaviour to test against - a human must pick one.

It is now BLOCKED on a named human actor and fully restated in REPORT.md § "Improvement run #3 — human-owned items, hand-off" (appended cycle 5, verified by the conductor). attempts stays 0: nothing was tried and failed, so an attempts bump would misreport the history. Unblocks the moment a human rules; nothing in the swarm can unblock it. CYCLE 6 CORROBORATION + one new fact. The cycle-6 QA live-look, an instrument with no knowledge of D-43, independently re-derived the empty-seed gap from the shipped binary and reached the same two-clauses-point-opposite-ways reading. Independent re-derivation raises confidence that this gap is real and human-owned, and it cost nothing to learn because the agent was not told the answer. NEW FACT for whoever rules, which D-43 does NOT record: the refusal is specific to EMPTY and WHITESPACE-ONLY values. Whitespace-PADDED values are ACCEPTED today — `node bin/aphorism.js --seed " 5 " --json` is byte-identical to `--seed 5` and exits 0 (conductor-measured, cycle 6, .swarm/runs/cycle-006-qa-verify.txt). So the implementation is not uniformly "trim then reject"; src/args.js:55 rejects only when the trimmed value is empty, then hands the UNTRIMMED string to Number(), which itself tolerates padding. A ruling of "accept per Number()" is therefore a smaller change than it looks: it deletes one guard clause rather than reworking seed parsing.

items.title: The --tag vocabulary is undiscoverable without jq, and an unknown tag is indistinguishable from an empty result
items.acceptance: BLOCKED ON A HUMAN SCOPE DECISION, not on engineering. The agent's remedy is a `--tags` flag, and 'any new flag' is a locked non-goal of this run; naming the valid tags on stderr also changes shipped behaviour. To unblock, the owner lifts the new-flag non-goal at a future kickoff. Until then only the DOCUMENTARY half is in scope, the same split TS-2 already carries: README and --help may list the twelve tag names inline instead of delegating discovery to a `--list --json | jq -r .tags[] | sort -u` pipeline.
items.notes: From the run #4 cycle-9 TASTE pass, finding 4 (minor). Adjacent to TS-2 but DISTINCT: TS-2 is about tag pool SIZE (five pools hold <= 4 entries), this is about the tag vocabulary being unDISCOVERABLE. CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED, gate cells E1/E2/E4 plus adjudication columns C/D/E/F: no --tags flag exists (`--tags` exits 2, --help never mentions it); --help does delegate discovery to a jq pipeline (measured line: `node bin/aphorism.js --list --json | jq -r '.tags[]' | sort -u`); and an unknown tag produces byte-identical stderr and exit status to a genuinely empty intersection of two VALID filters (`--tag performance --author "Martin Fowler"`), both exit 1 + 'aphorism: no aphorism matches those filters' + empty stdout. An unknown AUTHOR is indistinguishable too. The message is not merely generic across tags — it is generic across the entire no-match class, which is defensible unix behaviour and is why this is filed minor rather than as a bug. || RE-DERIVED at run #5 cycle 9; corroborated, not filed. Conductor gate cells B1/B2/C1 re-measured: `--tag testing` exits 1 with byte-exact stderr "aphorism: no aphorism matches those filters", the corpus has no "testing" tag but does have "debugging", and the message names neither the fold target nor the vocabulary; control cell B2 proves --tag itself works (`--tag debugging` exits 0), so B1's exit 1 is about the vocabulary and not a broken flag; C1 confirms --help still offers only a jq pipeline and no direct tag-listing flag. What this pass adds is the WORST-CASE instance: "testing" is the single most natural tag a first-timer types, it was DELIBERATELY folded into "debugging" by an earlier decision, and the tool knows the fold and says nothing. | carried into improvement run #6 unchanged; the brief forbids the ruling this needs

items.title: P-5 (green at every commit) and P-6 (the self-falsifying citation guard) are in direct conflict, and only a human can rule on which gives
items.acceptance: A human rules on ONE of: (a) P-5 wording is amended to exempt the single commit that introduces a src/bin/test/.github change from the full-clone green requirement, on the stated ground that the CI run which refreshes the citation cannot exist before the push; (b) the citation design changes so the window closes; or (c) the guard is retired. Until then the exception stands recorded, never re-labelled as a pass.
items.notes: MEASURED cycle 5, not inferred. P-6 mechanizes README Node-support own falsifier. Because the pathspec it cites is `src bin test .github`, ANY commit touching those paths makes the cited diff non-empty at that commit, so the suite is RED on a full clone until a follow-up commit re-cites to a CI run for it — and that CI run cannot exist until after the push. Commit 5f833ab is exactly that case: red on a full clone, green in CI (the guard skips on depth-1 checkout), repaired by c0337f1. P-5 requires green at >=119 on EVERY commit this run makes, so 5f833ab is a genuine exception and is recorded as one in .swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-P-6.txt. WHY THIS IS HUMAN-OWNED: every available disposition edits a locked SPEC must-have or deletes a shipped claim, and this run non-goals forbid the swarm doing either for itself. Note the window is not a defect in the test — it is the price of the claim being checkable at all, and the alternative (a citation nothing runs) is the state that let the claim go stale undetected two cycles ago. | cycle 10 SHARPENED THE CONFLICT WITHOUT RESOLVING IT. RF-5 made the guard fire on the WORKING TREE, so the exception is no longer discovered a cycle late by a full clone — it is now visible pre-commit, to the very run that causes it. That is strictly better for detection and it changes nothing about the disposition: the window between push and re-citation still exists and still violates "green at every commit", because CI cannot describe a commit that has not been pushed. Ruling (a)/(b)/(c) is still a human call, and it is now a call a human will meet on EVERY commit touching src/bin/test/.github rather than occasionally. | carried into improvement run #6 unchanged; the brief forbids the ruling this needs

items.title: Human ruling: is a coordinated table-wide falsification worth an out-of-document anchor?
items.acceptance: a human rules on whether the README matrix should be anchored to something outside the document, and if so which of the two mechanisms is acceptable
items.notes: Measured, not speculated — gate cell C7, cycle 4: changing all four rows TOGETHER to a self-consistent falsehood (200 tests, 198 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped) leaves the guard SILENT at 5 pass / 0 fail. The internal-consistency anchor cannot see a lie told consistently. Closing it needs an anchor OUTSIDE the document, and both options carry costs a swarm should not choose unilaterally: (1) live network provenance — makes an offline suite depend on GitHub and would SKIP in exactly the shallow-CI environment the table describes, i.e. inert where it is most needed; (2) a committed machine-readable CI artifact that the workflow writes and the guard reads — no network, but it adds a generated file to the repo and changes what CI is responsible for. BLOCKED on the operator, like P-7. Not a defect in Q-3, which never claimed this ground.

items.title: Retire the >=121 test-COUNT floor; replace it with a rerunnable DETECTION floor (bounded mutation harness)
items.acceptance: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs exists, is zero-dependency, runs via `node tools/mutation-matrix.mjs` from a clean tree, and is NOT part of test_cmd (adds zero tests). It enumerates a BOUNDED mutation set generated by a stated rule — exactly one falsifying mutation per machine-checked claim in the guarded README sections (off-by-one for each numeric claim, row-deletion for each structural table row the guards read), capped at 30, plus exactly ONE identity (no-op) mutation as converse control. The identity control must leave the suite GREEN. Any claim the generation rule produces but the harness omits is listed in the harness with its reason.
